rejoin_overlap_check: terminal_gateway.py and test_terminal_gateway_pty_io.py retained the same canonical blobs on main (3b1aa61e... and f7503cd7...), so intervening main changes did not overlap this repair
problem: The Clerk-authenticated WebSocket input path rechecked token expiry after receive, but the worker-thread PTY write loop carried no admitting auth deadline. A frame accepted just before exp could therefore continue through later partial os.write iterations after the Clerk lease expired.
counterhypothesis: Because PTY frames are bounded to 65536 bytes, os.write might normally complete immediately and the missing inner deadline check could be operationally irrelevant. This cannot be assumed: current code explicitly handles partial writes, so the security contract must remain correct under that already-admitted partial-write reality.

repair.terminal_gateway: freeze frame_auth_deadline from the lease that admitted each binary frame; pass that immutable deadline into _write_pty_all; check lease immediately before and after every kernel write so expiry cannot authorize later partial-write continuation or be reported as successful after a blocking syscall crosses the deadline
repair.reauth_semantics: reauth may extend future frames but does not retroactively extend an input frame already admitted under an older deadline
repair.tests: extend PTY I/O regressions for live partial completion, no-progress failure, expiry during a partial write, already-expired pre-write denial, and source binding of frame deadline into the worker-thread call
